title: Quarterly cadence and experiment plan for Dedicated capacity autoscaling
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Objective: Establish a repeatable quarterly cadence of prioritized experiments and rollouts that reduce unit inference cost while meeting latency SLOs for Dedicated customers. Background: customers increasingly use Reserved Dedicated capacity with burst/elastic needs. Current ad-hoc experiments have reduced cost in pockets but lack a standardized experiment-to-rollout path. Scope: define success metrics, run prioritized experiments (predictive prewarm, demand hedging, adaptive burst slabs, pool fairshare), instrument dashboards, and publish rollout/rollback runbooks. Out of scope: major scheduler/kernel rewrites; those will be separate ENG epics. Deliverables: 1) Experiment calendar for 12 weeks with owners; 2) Canary plan and rollback gates; 3) Dashboard views in Redwood Console showing per-pool prewarm hit rate, average p99 latency by model family, and cost per token delta; 4) Runbook for capacity hedging and surge fallback; 5) Postmortem template and evaluation rubric. Success metrics (quarter): - Latency SLOs: maintain p95 < configured SLO for 95% of traffic post-rollout; - Cost: achieve >= 8% unit-cost reduction on targeted workload slices without increasing error rate; - Reliability: reduce incidents caused by cold-starts by 50% for pilot customers; - Adoption: 3 enterprise customers opt-in to adaptive autoscale pilot. Acceptance criteria: production canary completes in two weeks with no SLO regression; dashboards surfaced for PM/Eng/SE; documented rollback steps and runbook approved by Platform OPS. Implementation phases: Phase A (Weeks 1-4) - baseline telemetry, small model-family experiments (predictive prewarm), define Canary metrics. Phase B (Weeks 5-8) - regional pilot with burst slabs, autoscale policy tuning, cost analysis. Phase C (Weeks 9-12) - enterprise pilot onboarding, runbook and org-wide playbook, release notes. Stakeholders: Product (Aisha Kapoor), Infra/Runtime ENG (Diego Martinez, Priya Shenoy), Platform Ops (Samir Patel), Solutions Engineering (Lina Chen), Design for console UX (Evan Brooks). Resource needs: 0.6 FTE PM, 1.4 FTE Eng for 3 months, priority access to Dedicated pool capacity for pilot customers, data analyst for dashboards. Risks & mitigations: - Cost spikes from over-provisioning: cap experimental warm pool size and use budget alarms; - SLO regression during kernel changes: require opt-in toggle and immediate rollback path; - Customer confusion with tier behavior: create clear customer-facing docs and opt-in contract language. Dependencies: ENG infra scheduling changes, Console dashboard tickets, billing telemetry updates. Next steps: confirm experiment owners, lock pilot customers, and schedule kickoff review with Ops and Sales by 2026-03-12.
